let's build a testing harness for another project that I'm calling standard-configuration. I want to be able to checkout a branch or commit of that project which is under ~/ai/standard-configuration, run a command in the project, and check that it did what I expected it to do. Some of those expectations will be simple (i.e. does this file exists? does it have this content? how long did it run for?) and some of those will be fuzzier and will need the use of an LLM-as-a-judge (i.e. does the output conform to the initial plan? run this generated script and test that *its* output is correct. etc...)

The standard-configuration will be spinning up agents to do the work in background processes, so we'll need to ensure we have a way of tracking that those processes are completed before evaluating the output. We should keep track of the start and end time of the whole thing.

The first thing I want to test is whether the standard-configuration project correctly executeds the project-init slash command, which should 1) create a README.md file, 2) create a github configuration that includes a main branch and a staging branch, 3) leaves us on the staging branch. Because standard-configuration is a git repo itself, we'll have to have the test remove git configuration before running this command. The command that should run the project-init function is something like `claude -p -- /project-init` but also include verbose, steam-json, a model selector, and any other necessary configs.

We should keep runs separated so that we can go into any run folder and explore the output of the system. Runs should have ids. Multiple runs per commit/project are possible. For example, we may want to evaluate different models.

We should keep track of everything related to runs and results in a sqlite database and artifact files where necessary. Let's set up a proper migrations flow for that.

Let's write this testing framework in python.

This does not make sense: claude -p --model gpt-4o. You cannot run claude with openai's models. For this task, let's run it with once with haiku and once with sonnet. In the future, I will specify the default model in some runners within the project, though, we'll still want to test multiple models.
